title: Roman Knights (the Equestrian Order)
lead: The Roman Knights were the wealthy class just below the senators. They ran the emperor's finances, commanded the Praetorian Guard, governed Egypt and sat on juries; Tacitus often names them beside the Senate.

sections.b: Wikipedia says an equestrian wore a gold ring on the left hand, and that Augustus' law let any Roman citizen assessed at a property of 100,000 denarii use the title and wear the ring. A denarius was four sesterces (Wikipedia, Denarius: 25 denarii equal 100 sestertii), so that is 400,000 sesterces; the conversion is my arithmetic. Offices open to Knights included command of the Praetorian Guard, the prefecture of Egypt and procurators of imperial provinces. Tacitus speaks of the leading Roman Knights sharing the Senate's joy at Nero's end (1:4), says Roman Knights governed Egypt from the time of Augustus (1:11), and says Icelus, Galba's freedman, was given the gold rings of a Roman Knight (1:13).
